items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: I’d take “Four Brothers,” from Woody Herman.

ctx.x: I think I know what you mean. Monterey.

Monterey. Thank you. The Monterey Jazz Party, and I went out to go to the bathroom and when I came back in there was this terrible noise. Woody Herman’s band was there, and the Ellington band was there, and a lot of great guys. And there was this terrible sound and this guy up there with a white plastic saxophone. And I thought for God’s sakes, what’s going on here? And that was Ornette Coleman. First time I’d heard him. And it just didn’t make any sense to me. Still doesn’t. But people like me are dying off.…
Well he was innovating but what he was innovating was—
